questions.answer: Postquam mīlitēs urbem cēperint, rēgīnam captīvam dūcent.

questions.prompt: He himself, inflamed with crime and fury, came into the forum; his eyes were blazing, cruelty stood out from his whole face.
questions.answer: Ipse īnflammātus scelere et furōre in forum vēnit; ārdēbant oculī, tōtō ex ōre crūdēlitās ēminēbat.

questions.prompt: That was the road I was trying, cautiously, step by step.
questions.answer: Eam egō̆ viam pedetemptim temptābam.

questions.prompt: The senate knows this, the consul sees it, yet this man lives.
questions.answer: Senātus haec intellegit, cōnsul videt, hīc tamen vīvit.

questions.prompt: I give you my seat.
questions.answer: Tibi concēdō meās sēdīs.

questions.prompt: You arrange a case, he arrays an army.
questions.answer: Tū āctiōnem īnstituis, ille aciem īnstruit.

questions.prompt: Epicurus says such things.
questions.answer: Epicūrus vērō ea dīcit.

questions.prompt: For a long time I have not known what you were doing.
questions.answer: Iam diū īgnōrō quid agās.

questions.prompt: I have long been urging you.
questions.answer: Tē iam dūdum hortor.

questions.prompt: We suffer now these many years. We no longer suffer.
questions.answer: Patimur multōs iam annōs.

questions.prompt: For a year you have been a hearer of Cratippus.
questions.answer: Annum iam audīs Cratippum.

questions.prompt: So far Plancius has kept me here.
questions.answer: Adhūc Plancius mē retinet.

questions.prompt: I move for fifty days' thanksgiving.
questions.answer: Dēcernō quīnquāgintā diērum supplicātiōnēs.

questions.prompt: Rome meanwhile grows as a result of the fall of Alba: the number of citizens is doubled; the Coelian hill is added to the town.
questions.answer: Rōma interim crēscit Albae ruīnīs: duplicātur cīvium numerus; Caelius additur urbī mōns.

questions.prompt: Was I trying to send into exile one who I saw had already gone into war?
questions.answer: In exsilium ēiciēbam quem iam ingressum esse in bellum vidēbam?

questions.prompt: They were coming if it had been allowed.
questions.answer: Sī licitum esset veniēbant.

questions.prompt: For, you know, while I was with you, you could not see my soul.
questions.answer: Nec enim dum eram vōbīscum animum meum vidēbātis.

questions.prompt: Lentulus was bold enough as an orator, but could not endure the exertion of thinking hard.
questions.answer: Lentulus satis erat fortis ōrātōr, sed cōgitandī nōn ferēbat labōrem.

questions.prompt: This day has put an end to my long-continued silence.
questions.answer: Diūturnī silentī fīnem hodiernus diēs attulit.

questions.prompt: So great a war he made ready for at the end of winter, undertook in early spring, and finished by midsummer.
questions.answer: Tantum bellum extrēmā hieme apparāvit, ineunte vēre suscēpit, mediā aestāte cōnfēcit.

questions.prompt: Those who have always been in the fetters of the body, even when released move more slowly.
questions.answer: Quī in compedibus corporis semper fuērunt, etiam cum solūtī sunt tardius ingrediuntur.

questions.prompt: There was once such virtue in this commonwealth.
questions.answer: Fuit ista quondam in hāc rē pūblicā virtūs.

questions.prompt: This was the nature of the ground which our men had chosen for a camp.
questions.answer: Locī nātūra erat haec, quem locum nostrī castrīs dēlēgerant.

questions.prompt: As you sow.
questions.answer: Ut sēmentem fēceris, ita metēs.

questions.prompt: When the plots of that man have been shown to be as clear as daylight, then, and not till then, shall I conjure you.
questions.answer: Sī illīus īnsidiae clāriōrēs hāc lūce fuerint, tum dēnique obsecrābō.

questions.prompt: I at least shall have done my duty.
questions.answer: Ego certē meum officium praestiterō.

questions.prompt: What has been found out I shall see presently.
questions.answer: Quid inventum sit paulō post vīderō.

questions.prompt: Whoever crushes (shall have crushed) Antony will finish (will have finished) a most loathsome war.
questions.answer: Quī Antōnium oppresserit bellum taeterrimum cōnfēcerit.

questions.prompt: I answered all your letters yesterday.
questions.answer: Ad tuās omnīs [epistulās] rescrīpseram prīdiē.
